title: Rovaniemi's protected riverside block is becoming a hotel
seoTitle: Rovaniemi riverside block becomes a hotel
description: Rovaniemi's protected Lääninhallitus block is being turned into a hotel of about 100 rooms. According to Lapin Kansa it is planned to open in summer 2028.
dek: Partition walls are already coming out of the main building, and the opening is now planned for summer 2028; in March the estimate was October 2027.
heroAlt: Rovaniemi city centre on a dark October evening: the lit entrance of the Sampokeskus shopping centre, a tall advertising pillar in the middle of the square and a few people walking across the empty paving.
heroCaption: Rovaniemi city centre on an October evening in 2026. The Lääninhallitus block stands in the same city centre, on the bank of the Kemijoki between the Jätkänkynttilä and Ounaskoski bridges.

body.text: Work has started to turn the historic Lääninhallitus block in Rovaniemi into a hotel. For travellers it changes nothing this winter or the next, as no rooms are on sale yet.

body.title: The hotel project in brief
items: Owner of the block: City-Hotelli Oy, a Rovaniemi family company
Purchase price: 4.5 million euros according to Yle
Working name of the hotel: Arctic Garden

body.text: According to Lapin Kansa the work is first concentrated on the main building of the provincial government, where the partition walls between office rooms are being pulled down to make way for hotel rooms.

The owner is City-Hotelli Oy, a Rovaniemi family company that already runs Arctic City Hotel and Arctic Light Hotel in the town. It bought the block from the state property company Senaatti-kiinteistöt in March 2026, and according to Yle the price was 4.5 million euros.

The working name of the new hotel is Arctic Garden, although Mikael Gröhn has said it may also become Arctic Avenue. The family says it wants to keep the history of the protected buildings visible and to open the park-like block to the people of Rovaniemi again.
A block that has stood almost unchanged

The block, known as Koskenranta, lies on the bank of the Kemijoki between the Jätkänkynttilä and Ounaskoski bridges. According to Senaatti-kiinteistöt the provincial government office building was completed in 1947 and the house of the Kemijoki floating association in 1939.

The floating association house is the oldest building on the site and the only one that survived the destruction of the Lapland War. The block also holds the governor's residence, its sauna and outbuilding, a terraced house built for civil servants and the old heating plant.
The whole is part of the Poronsarvi town plan drawn by Alvar Aalto, which set the shape of Rovaniemi's administrative and cultural centre after the Second World War.

Senaatti-kiinteistöt says the built environment has stayed practically unchanged for almost seventy years and that most of the buildings and their yards were protected by a decision of the Lapland ELY Centre in 2025. The rooms have been empty since the Regional State Administrative Agency for Lapland moved out in 2024.
Suites, a restaurant and a sauna

Mikael Gröhn said in March that the three apartments of more than 100 square metres in the riverside house will become villa-type hotel suites, that the governor's representative rooms may be taken into use as an event space and that the round-log guest house could serve as the hotel's private sauna.
The restaurant is planned for the ballroom, which would be extended with a glass annex in the same way as at Arctic Light Hotel.

The company says the buildings keep their original exterior and that only the interiors are adapted to hotel use. Senaatti-kiinteistöt had already emptied the rooms of their original furniture and light fittings, and those cannot be brought back, so the hotel is to be furnished in the spirit of the buildings instead.
The courtyard park is meant for everyone

The park of nearly two hectares inside the block is the part Gröhn calls the heart of the project. The plans include paths, places to sit and food and drink served outdoors, and details such as the Äiti-Lappi statue are to be kept. In winter the company wants snow, ice and lighting to turn the yard into what it calls the city's living room.
Nothing to book yet
For a traveller the block changes nothing this winter or the next. No rooms are on sale, and on its own site the company says the project timeline is still being refined and gives no opening date.

According to Lapin Kansa the hotel is planned to open in summer 2028, while according to Yle the estimate given when the deal was signed in March was October 2027. A zoning amendment started in 2018 is also still pending for the area.
Until the block opens, the same family's two hotels in the centre are the ones that can be booked.

items: Arctic Light Hotel: 57 rooms in a building designed by the architect Ferdinand Salokangas
Arctic City Hotel: open since 1978, with 55 Classic rooms, 33 Style rooms and two junior suites with a sauna

body.text: A hotel that opens in 2028 does not help with this winter's rooms, so the choice of area matters more right now. You can find the hotels in Rovaniemi by area, from the centre to the Arctic Circle, on our Rovaniemi page.
